newsitem.title: UK: Ekofisk loadings delayed on Fulmar tie-in hitch.
newsitem.headline: Ekofisk loadings delayed on Fulmar tie-in hitch.

text.p: Delays in commissioning a pipeline tie-in of the UK North Sea Fulmar oilfield to Norway's Ekofisk stream via the Norpipe system has delayed February Ekofisk loadings, traders said on Wednesday.
Liftings of Ekofisk from Britain's Teeside terminal, due for a boost from the Fulmar tie-in, were being postponed by about six days, the traders said.

Fulmar operator Shell Expro, which operates in the North sea on behalf of Shell and Exxon Corp, said commissioning of the pipeline was still underway, leaving the flow of Fulmar into Norpipe variable.
"Commissioning is continuing. It's up and down," said a Shell spokesman.
"It will probably mean a change in some dates for Ekofisk," said a trader at an Ekofisk equity holder.
Most Fulmar loadings continue via the old method of offshore tanker liftings and there was no impact on overall Fulmar output, the Shell spokesman said.
The delayed tie-in has forced a U.S. refiner scheduled to load one million barrels of mid-month Ekofisk back to the market in search of a million-barrel Brent cargo, said.

A week's shutdown in mid-January at the 350,000 bpd Ekofisk field due to a gas leak in an oil pipeline in mid-January already delayed the start of the February loading schedule until about February 10.
Ekofisk in February is scheduled to load 26 cargoes totalling 14.1 million barrels.
